Fact.Name: Eligible child year of birth (Form 8839 Part I line 1 column (b))
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "In what year was this child born?" — the four digit calendar year printed in this child's Part I row, column (b). HELP: the form asks for the YEAR only, never a full date, which is why this is an Int rather than a Day; enter the year of birth even for an adoption that was unsuccessful or is not yet final. ASKED WHEN: once per item in /form8839Children, on the Part I identity screen beside the child's name and identifying number; it is a printed cell of every Part I row, so it is asked for every child. VALIDATION: a four digit calendar year. UNANSWERED (three-state): the printed box stays blank and ../childAgeEligible falls back to TRUE, because losing a credit on silence is the taxpayer-adverse direction — but the blank is NOT free, see below. CONSUMER AND MONEY CONSEQUENCE: ../childAgeEligible reads this year and is true for 2007 or later (a child born in 2007 turned 18 during 2025 and is an eligible child for the part of the year they were under 18). A year of 2006 or earlier fails the under-18 half of the eligible-child definition, and unless column (c) (../writableChildBornBefore2008AndDisabled) is checked, ../childMeetsEligibleChildDefinition is false and ../line2 — with line 4, line 6, line 10, line 11a and line 11b behind it — is $0 for this child. Leaving the box blank on a child who does compute a Part II credit is the case this module cannot resolve on its own: the credit is granted today on a question the filer was never asked, and the successor named on ../childAgeEligible is a submission refusal for exactly that state, owed and not yet built. So this question must be put to the filer whenever the child has qualified expenses, and it must not be left to the default.

Fact.Name: The adoption expenses entered for this child were paid before the child turned 18
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Were the adoption expenses you entered for this child paid before the child turned 18? Enter only such expenses." HELP: a child who turned 18 is an eligible child for the part of the year the child was under 18, so expenses paid before the 18th birthday count even when they reach this return in a later year. ASKED WHEN: this child's year of birth is 2006 (a domestic or foreign child), or earlier for a foreign child (column (e) checked), and column (c) is not checked. VALIDATION: Yes / No. UNANSWERED or No: ../childAgeEligible stays false for such a child, as before. Feeds ../childAgeEligible.

Fact.Name: Your agreed share of the $17,280 exclusion limit for this child (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's agreed share of the $17,280 per-child exclusion limit when a non-spouse also received employer-provided adoption benefits for THIS same child (../writableSharesExclusionLimitWithNonSpouse). i8839 Line 19: "You can divide it in any way you both agree. Enter your share of the $17,280 limit on line 19 for that child." Unanswered resolves to $0 through ../dividedExclusionShare, never to the full limit.

Fact.Name: Prior year employer-provided adoption benefits for this child (Form 8839 line 20)
Fact.Description: If employer-provided adoption benefits were received in a prior year for THIS same child, the total of the amounts shown on lines 20 and 24 (or corresponding lines) of the last Form 8839 filed for the child, entered in this child's line 20 column. Asked only when /writableAdoptionReceivedPriorYearEmployerBenefits is true.

Fact.Name: Employer has a qualified adoption assistance program, complete safe (i8839 Line 24)
Fact.Description: = /writableAdoptionEmployerHasQualifiedAssistanceProgram when answered, else false. False is the conservative default: without the program the special needs full amount arm of line 24 does not apply and the taxpayer must enter the smaller of line 21 or line 22, which is the SMALLER exclusion and therefore the larger taxable benefit. Never asked means never over excluded.

Fact.Name: Modified adjusted gross income for the adoption exclusion (Form 8839 line 25)
Fact.Description:
Form 8839 line 25 MAGI, which is NOT the Form 8839 line 7 MAGI: i8839 prints a separate Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) Worksheet for line 25 and warns "Your MAGI for the adoption credit may not be the same as the MAGI figured in the above worksheet." The body is that worksheet's own shape. It reads income:/totalIncomeDisregardingSection137 (the worksheet's lines 1 + 2 + 3: Form 1040 line 1z carrying the full Form 8839 line 23 rather than the line 31 remainder, plus the other income lines and Schedule 1 line 10), subtracts taxCalculations:/adjustmentsToIncomeExcludingStudentLoanInterest (worksheet line 5, which omits Schedule 1 line 21 and therefore never subtracts the student loan interest deduction in the first place) and adds the three exclusions the worksheet's footer names (Form 2555, Form 4563 and Puerto Rico). It does not route through taxCalculations:/agi, and studentLoanAdjustment:/studentLoanInterestAdjustmentAmount is not in its upstream cone, so neither return arc on /adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits exists.
WHY THE BASE DISREGARDS SECTION 137 RATHER THAN SUBTRACTING LINE 31 BACK OUT. The amount subtracted would itself be downstream of this fact, so the subtraction would cancel the value and keep the edge. The worksheet removes the benefits from line 1z by construction for exactly this reason, and sections 86(b)(2)(A) and 219(g)(3)(A)(ii) make the same figure the right base for the social security and IRA MAGIs, so one income-side quantity serves all three.
TERRITORY RETURNS. On the section 931/933 population this body's adjustments total is the unapportioned Schedule 1 figure (worksheet line 5, "Schedule 1 lines 11 through 20, 23, and 25" as filed), not the Pub 1321 apportioned total, so this MAGI can be LOWER (less phaseout, more exclusion, taxpayer-favourable) on a territory return carrying Schedule 1 adjustments. It is the worksheet's own line 5 verbatim, so it is the defended reading.

Fact.Name: Form 8839 line 26 No: Part III modified AGI is not more than the phaseout threshold
Fact.Description: The negation of /adoptionExclusionMagiOverPhaseoutThreshold, and the printed No box on line 26: skip lines 26 and 27 and enter $0 on line 28. Exactly one of the pair is true on every return.

Fact.Name: Form 8839 line 26 Yes: Part III modified AGI is more than the phaseout threshold
Fact.Description: The printed answer to Form 8839 line 26, "Is line 25 more than $259,190?". True when /adoptionExclusionMagi (line 25, the Part III modified AGI) is greater than /adoptionPhaseoutThreshold, which is the Yes branch that subtracts the threshold from line 25 onto line 26. It is the Part III twin of the line 8 pair and restates the comparison /adoptionExclusionPhaseoutExcessBeforeFloor already makes.

Fact.Name: Line 25 MAGI over the phaseout threshold, before the zero floor (Form 8839 line 26)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 26 before the floor = line 25 (/adoptionExclusionMagi) minus $259,190 (/adoptionPhaseoutThreshold, the same threshold the credit uses on line 8). Negative for a filer below the threshold; /adoptionLine26PhaseoutExcess applies the floor the printed No branch describes ("Skip lines 26 and 27, and enter -0- on line 28").

Fact.Name: Zero floor for the Form 8839 line 26 excess
Fact.Description: The $0 floor the printed No branch of line 26 produces. A structural literal, not a statutory amount: it exists so /adoptionLine26PhaseoutExcess can be a GreaterOf over a Dollar fact.

Fact.Name: Adoption exclusion phaseout fraction x1000 (Form 8839 line 27)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 27 = line 26 divided by $40,000, rounded to three places and never more than 1.000, represented here as INTEGER THOUSANDTHS exactly as /adoptionPhaseoutFractionThousandths represents line 9. 0 below the threshold, 1000 (= 1.000) at or above $299,190 of line 25 MAGI. Per return: consumed by EVERY child's line 28 as line 24 x (this / 1000), matching "Multiply each amount on line 24 by line 27". This is the fact behind the printed line 27, but it is NOT what either printed line 27 box holds: the form splits the decimal into an integer box and a three digit fractional box, and no Dollar can print 050 into the fractional box.

Fact.Name: Form 8839 line 27 ratio in thousandths, before the 1.000 cap
Fact.Description: Line 26 divided by $40,000, carried as INTEGER THOUSANDTHS (the decimal times 1,000) so it can be an exact Dollar value: Round(line 26 x 1000 / 40000). $0 when line 25 does not exceed the threshold. /adoptionExclusionPhaseoutFractionThousandths then applies the printed 1.000 cap.

Fact.Name: Total employer-provided adoption benefits received in 2025 (Form 8839 line 23)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 23 = "Add the amounts on line 22" = the sum across children of the 2025 employer-provided adoption benefits. Per return. Gated on IsComplete(/form8839Children) for the same reason /adoptionLine11cRefundable is: CollectionSum over an undeclared collection would resolve Incomplete and cascade through lines 25, 30 and 31 on every return that has no Form 8839 at all.

Fact.Name: Line 25 MAGI over the phaseout threshold (Form 8839 line 26)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 26 = the amount by which line 25 exceeds $259,190, floored at $0. The Yes branch prints the subtraction; the No branch skips lines 26 and 27 and enters -0- on line 28, which the floor reproduces (a $0 excess makes line 27 zero and line 28 zero). The printed box is left blank on the No branch rather than showing 0; a $0 fact prints a zero there, the one cosmetic difference.

Fact.Name: Total excluded employer-provided adoption benefits (Form 8839 line 30)
Fact.Description:
Form 8839 line 30 = "Add the amounts on line 29" = the total employer-provided adoption benefits excluded from gross income for 2025, across all eligible children. Gated on IsComplete(/form8839Children) for the same reason /adoptionLine11cRefundable is.
FILING-STATUS GATE. A leading case zeroes this line for a filer whose filing status does not permit the exclusion at all: i8839's "Who Can Take the Adoption Credit or Exclude Employer-Provided Adoption Benefits?" statement (1) governs BOTH halves of this form in one sentence, and IRC 137(e) carries the section 23(f)(1) joint-return requirement onto the exclusion. Both halves read the one predicate /adoptionFilingStatusEligible.
Line 31 = line 23 minus this line, and line 31 is Form 1040 line 1f, so an unentitled exclusion here would walk straight out of /agi. Zeroing line 30 makes line 31 equal line 23, which is the printed arithmetic for a filer who may exclude nothing: the whole employer-provided benefit is taxable. Line 23 is deliberately NOT gated (the money was still received) and line 31 is deliberately NOT gated (the gate belongs where the exclusion is computed, and gating the subtraction would leave the Yes-branch negative reachable for a filer with no exclusion).
COMPLETE-SAFE: the eligibility fact resolves Complete on every return that ANSWERS a filing status, and the leading When is All(IsComplete(eligible), Not(eligible)), the canonical negated complete-safe form, so an unanswered filing status falls through to the cases below (catch-all $0) instead of turning this line, line 31 or Form 1040 line 1z Placeholder.
THE GATE IS ALSO ON LINE 29, and this case is KEPT there and here. With the same All(IsComplete(eligible), Not(eligible)) case on /form8839Children/*/line29, this line falls out by its own printed rule for a barred filer. Keeping this case as well is deliberate belt-and-braces: it makes the $0 hold by this fact's own body whatever the collection's state (declared, empty or absent), so lines 30 and 31 are byte-identical structurally rather than through the sum. Both cases read the ONE predicate /adoptionFilingStatusEligible, which is what the C4 extraction was for, so this is a second reader and not a second source of truth.

Fact.Name: Form 8839 line 31 No: excluded benefits are not more than total employer benefits
Fact.Description: The negation of /adoptionLine30OverLine23, and the printed No box on line 31: subtract line 30 from line 23 and, if more than zero, include the result on line 1f of Form 1040. Exactly one of the pair is true on every return.

Fact.Name: Form 8839 line 31 Yes: excluded benefits are more than total employer benefits
Fact.Description: The printed answer to Form 8839 line 31, "Is line 30 more than line 23?". True when /adoptionLine30ExcludedBenefits is greater than /adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits, the Yes branch that subtracts line 23 from line 30 and enters the result as a negative number. That negative case is real: a special needs adoption may exclude the full per child limit even when the employer paid less, which is why /adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits can be negative.

Fact.Name: Pre-2025 employer benefits included in Form 8839 line 22, all children (worksheet line 5)
Fact.Description: Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet line 5 = the sum across /form8839Children of ../foreignRoutePriorYearBenefitsOnLine22 — the pre-2025 money the worksheet route brought into this year's line 22. The multi-child rule is why this is a RETURN-level sum over PER-CHILD lines 1 to 3: "If the adoption of more than one eligible foreign child became final in 2025, complete lines 1 through 3 … separately for each foreign child and use the combined totals to complete lines 4 through 9." GATED on IsComplete(/form8839Children) for the reason /adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits states: a bare CollectionSum over the undeclared collection every non-adoption return has resolves Incomplete and would cascade into line 31 and Form 1040 line 1z.

Fact.Name: This return takes the Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet
Fact.Description: True when any eligible child on the return is on the worksheet route, which is exactly the state in which worksheet line 5 is positive. Selects worksheet line 6 as Form 8839 line 31 in place of the ordinary line 23 minus line 30. COMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION: a GreaterThan over the gated worksheet line 5, which is $0 rather than Incomplete on a return with no declared children — so a return that answers none of the route questions resolves this Complete false, never Placeholder, and Form 8839 line 31 keeps its ordinary body.

Fact.Name: Form 8839 line 23 over line 30, floored at zero (worksheet line 4)
Fact.Description: Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet line 4 = Form 8839 line 23 minus line 30 when line 30 is less than line 23, and nothing at all otherwise ("No. Skip lines 4 through 6 of this worksheet and go to line 7"). The floor at $0 IS that No branch: on it, line 6 would be a subtraction from an amount the worksheet never wrote, and the taxable-benefits answer the worksheet produces is none — which is what a $0 line 4 carries into line 6.

Fact.Name: Taxable benefits on the prior-year-benefits route (worksheet line 6, Form 8839 line 31)
Fact.Description: Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet line 6 = line 4 minus line 5, floored: "Taxable benefits. Subtract line 5 of this worksheet from line 4. If zero or less, enter -0-. Enter the result here and on Form 8839, line 31." The floor is printed, and it is the whole point of the route: the pre-2025 benefits the filer brought into line 22 are subtracted back out of the taxable remainder, so the same dollars are not taxed in the year they were received and again in the year of finality.

Fact.Name: 2025 employer benefits included in Form 8839 line 22, all children (worksheet line 8)
Fact.Description: Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet line 8 = "the total 2025 employer-provided adoption benefits included on Form 8839, line 22, for all children" = the sum across /form8839Children of ../employerAdoptionBenefitsReceivedIn2025. EVERY child counts, not only route children: line 22 carries every child's 2025 benefits, and the worksheet says "for all children". Gated on IsComplete(/form8839Children) for the same reason worksheet line 5 is.

Fact.Name: Prior year excluded benefits (worksheet line 9, REPORTED)
Fact.Description:
Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet line 9 = line 7 (Form 8839 line 30) minus line 8, floored: "Prior year excluded benefits. Subtract line 8 of this worksheet from line 7. If zero or less, stop; you can't exclude any of your prior year benefits." It is how much of the pre-2025 benefits the section 137 exclusion actually reached this year. Worksheet line 7 is Form 8839 line 30 verbatim ("Enter the amount from Form 8839, line 30"), so it is read here directly rather than copied into a second fact.
REPORTED ONLY. Nothing on the 2025 return consumes this figure — the taxable side is line 6, which is Form 8839 line 31 — and the graph applies nothing to a prior year: a filer who excluded less in an earlier year does not amend anything from this number. It exists because the worksheet computes it and a filer keeping the worksheet needs it.

Fact.Name: Dollars answered on Form 8839 line 20 by children the worksheet forces to zero, all children
Fact.Description: The sum across /form8839Children of ../foreignRouteLine20AnsweredExposure. Gated on IsComplete(/form8839Children) for the reason /adoptionUnattestedEmployerReimbursementExposure states: a bare CollectionSum over an undeclared collection resolves Incomplete, and here that would cascade into a submission refusal.

Fact.Name: Refusal: a prior-year-benefits route child also answered Form 8839 line 20
Fact.Description:
At least one child takes the Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet route AND carries a positive Form 8839 line 20 (prior year benefits already excluded for the same child on an earlier Form 8839). The two answers cannot both be true. The worksheet forces line 20 to zero for a route child in terms — "Enter -0- on Form 8839, line 20" — and the reason is substantive: the adoption became final in 2025, so no earlier Form 8839 for this child could have excluded anything, section 23(e)(1) having barred the exclusion until finality. A positive line 20 therefore means either the finality answer or the line 20 amount is wrong, and the graph cannot tell which; excluding the same prior-year dollars twice, once through line 20 and once through the worksheet, is what silence here would buy.
AN INPUT CONTRADICTION, not a scope gap: nothing is unbuilt behind it, and correcting either answer clears it. COMPLETE-FALSE, never Incomplete, on every return that does not take the route: the aggregation is gated on IsComplete(/form8839Children) and each per-child term is a Switch whose route case is Complete by construction.

Fact.Name: Taxable employer-provided adoption benefits (Form 8839 line 31)
Fact.Description:
Form 8839 line 31 = line 23 minus line 30: the employer-provided adoption benefits that the section 137 exclusion does not reach and that therefore stay in gross income. The form splits this into two printed branches, No (line 30 not more than line 23, subtract line 30 from line 23) and Yes (line 30 more than line 23, subtract line 23 from line 30 and enter the result as a negative number). A single Subtract of line 30 from line 23 produces BOTH: it is positive on the No branch and negative on the Yes branch, which is exactly the sign the Yes branch asks for. CONSUMED BY FORM 1040 LINE 1f: income:/primaryFilerEmployerProvidedAdoptionBenefits and its secondary twin apportion this amount across the filers in proportion to their Form W-2 box 12 code T totals, defaulting the whole of it to the primary filer when no W-2 reports code T, so it reaches total income and AGI. Line 1f is SIGNED, the section 137(a)(2) special-needs mechanism, so the Yes branch's negative is carried as printed and is not floored. The direct wire was CIRCULAR until the MAGI base disregarding section 137 existed; the measurement that established that constraint is recorded below and is what the base was built against.
ON THE EXCLUSION OF PRIOR YEAR BENEFITS ROUTE this line is not line 23 minus line 30 at all: it is the worksheet's line 6, "Taxable benefits. Subtract line 5 of this worksheet from line 4. If zero or less, enter -0-. Enter the result here and on Form 8839, line 31", floored at $0. That is the printed instruction for a foreign child whose adoption became final in 2025 and for whom employer-provided benefits were received before 2025: the pre-2025 dollars enter line 22 and line 23, and worksheet line 5 takes them back out of the taxable remainder, so they are not taxed twice. The selector is /adoptionForeignPriorYearBenefitsRouteApplies, which is Complete-false on every return that answers none of the route questions, so the ordinary arm is unchanged for everyone else. The printed Yes-branch negative cannot arise from the route child itself, whose ../line24FullExclusionArmApplies is false (a foreign child is never a child with special needs, section 23(d)(3)(C)); it can still arise from a DIFFERENT, domestic special-needs child on the same return whose ../line24FullExclusionArmApplies is TRUE, and whose line 29 therefore adds to line 30 without adding a penny to line 23. That MIXED case is why the route arm is not worksheet line 6 alone but the SMALLER of worksheet line 6 and (line 23 minus line 30). Worksheet line 6 is bounded above by its own line 4, which is line 23 minus line 30 floored at $0, so wherever line 30 is below line 23 the LesserOf returns worksheet line 6 unchanged and the route is exactly as the worksheet prints it. Where line 30 EXCEEDS line 23 the worksheet's line 4 sends the filer past lines 4 through 6 without saying anything about line 31 ("No. Skip lines 4 through 6 of this worksheet and go to line 7"), and the printed answer is the form's own Yes branch: "Subtract line 23 from line 30. Enter the result as a negative number. Also, enter the result on line 1f of Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR." The LesserOf returns exactly that negative, signed, which is the section 137(a)(2) special-needs mechanism reaching Form 1040 line 1f. A floor at $0 here would silently drop it.

Fact.Name: Adoption exclusion MAGI phaseout range (Form 8839 line 27)
Fact.Description: The $40,000 phaseout range the form divides by on line 27, the same range line 9 uses for the credit. The exclusion is fully phased out at $299,190 of line 25 MAGI.

Fact.Name: No employer-provided adoption benefits in a prior year for the same child (Form 8839 line 20 No box)
Fact.Description: The No box of Form 8839 line 20 = Not(/writableAdoptionReceivedPriorYearEmployerBenefits). Because the underlying question is not complete safe, this fact is Incomplete until the taxpayer answers, so neither the No nor the Yes box is checked on an unanswered return, and exactly one is checked once the question is answered. The printed instruction on the No branch is "No. Enter -0-.", which is what /form8839Children/*/priorYearEmployerBenefits resolves to.

Fact.Name: Thousandths scale for the Form 8839 line 27 decimal
Fact.Description: The constant 1,000 used to carry the line 27 decimal as an integer number of thousandths, the same encoding /adoptionPhaseoutFractionThousandths uses for line 9. A rate encoding, declared structural: it is not a statutory amount. Used twice, as the numerator scale that turns line 26 divided by $40,000 into thousandths and as the divisor that turns those thousandths back into a fraction on line 28.

Fact.Name: Your agreed share of the $17,280 exclusion limit, complete safe (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description: = ../writableDividedExclusionShare when answered, else $0. The conservative default when a divided exclusion is asserted but no share is entered: a $0 share understates the exclusion rather than handing the taxpayer the full $17,280 that i8839 Line 19 says must be split.

Fact.Name: Employer-provided adoption benefits for this child, complete safe (Form 8839 line 22)
Fact.Description:
Form 8839 line 22 as PRINTED for this child. Ordinarily the 2025 benefits alone (../employerAdoptionBenefitsReceivedIn2025, which is ../writableEmployerAdoptionBenefits when answered and $0 otherwise), so an unanswered column cannot make line 23, line 30 or line 31 resolve Incomplete.
ON THE EXCLUSION OF PRIOR YEAR BENEFITS ROUTE it is the 2025 benefits PLUS the pre-2025 benefits for that foreign child, because the worksheet says so in terms: "On Form 8839, line 22, enter the total amount of employer-provided adoption benefits received in 2025 and all prior years." That is section 23(e)(2) as section 137(e) carries it: benefits received before the year of finality are taken into account as if received in that year. The addition is made on THIS wrapper rather than on the writable so that everything reading the printed line 22 - ../line24SmallerArm, ../hasUnattestedEmployerReimbursement, ../unattestedEmployerReimbursementExposure and /adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits, which is in turn what the formW2s box-12 code-T reconciliation reads - keeps reading one fact, and so that worksheet line 8 still has the 2025-only figure to sum.

Fact.Name: This foreign child's adoption became final DURING 2025 (Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet)
Fact.Description:
SCREEN SPEC. Ask: "Did this child's adoption become final during 2025?" HELP TEXT: Form 8839 Part I column (g) asks only whether the adoption was final "in 2025 OR EARLIER", and the Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet applies to a narrower group — a foreign child whose adoption became final IN 2025 (i8839 lines 375-376). Only that year of finality pulls the benefits received in earlier years into 2025, so the two questions cannot share one answer and this one is asked separately.
ASKED WHEN Part I columns (e) AND (g) are both checked for this child (../writableChildIsForeignChild and ../writableChildAdoptionFinalIn2025OrEarlier both true). Not asked for a domestic child, and not asked for a foreign child whose adoption is not yet final — that child is barred outright by ../childForeignAndNotFinal.
UNANSWERED (three-state) = FALSE = the ORDINARY route: the exclusion is figured on the 2025 benefits alone, this child's line 20 keeps whatever was entered, and no prior-year benefit is ever excluded. That is the ADVERSE direction, and it is chosen deliberately: a filer with pre-2025 benefits who is never asked LOSES worksheet line 9 and pays tax on benefits section 137 would have let them exclude. The favourable silence — granting the prior-year exclusion from a blank — is the one this form may not take.
FEEDS ../childOnForeignPriorYearBenefitsRoute, which selects the worksheet route on lines 19, 20 and 22 and, through /adoptionForeignPriorYearBenefitsRouteApplies, on line 31.

Fact.Name: This child's adoption became final during 2025, complete-safe
Fact.Description: = ../writableChildAdoptionBecameFinalDuring2025 when answered, else FALSE. The adverse default: an unanswered year of finality cannot prove the worksheet's population, so the child takes the ordinary route and no prior-year benefit is excluded. Complete on every declared item by construction, so the route predicate built on it is never Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Employer-provided adoption benefits received BEFORE 2025 for this foreign child (worksheet line 1, prior-years half)
Fact.Description:
SCREEN SPEC. Ask: "How much in employer-provided adoption benefits did you receive BEFORE 2025 for this child's adoption?" HELP TEXT: worksheet line 1 asks for "the total employer-provided adoption benefits you received in 2025 AND ALL PRIOR YEARS for the adoption of the foreign child" (i8839 lines 377-378); this question collects the prior-years half, and ../writableEmployerAdoptionBenefits (Form 8839 line 22 as it is ordinarily entered) collects the 2025 half. Because the adoption became final in 2025, section 23(e)(2) — carried onto the exclusion by section 137(e) — treats those earlier amounts as if they had been received in 2025, which is why they enter this year's line 22 rather than the prior year's.
ASKED WHEN this child's finality-in-2025 answer is yes. Integer cents; Min $0.
UNANSWERED (three-state) = $0 = the ORDINARY route, and that costs money: the route never opens, the prior-year benefits are never brought into line 22, and worksheet line 9 (the prior-year benefits the filer could have excluded) is never figured. A filer with pre-2025 benefits who is not asked loses that exclusion. The direction is ADVERSE, which is the direction the doctrine permits; the favourable alternative — inferring an amount, or excluding prior-year benefits from a blank — is not available.
FEEDS worksheet line 1 through ../employerAdoptionBenefits (Form 8839 line 22), the route predicate ../childOnForeignPriorYearBenefitsRoute, and worksheet line 5 through ../foreignRoutePriorYearBenefitsOnLine22.

Fact.Name: Pre-2025 employer benefits for this foreign child, complete-safe (worksheet line 1, prior-years half)
Fact.Description: = ../writablePriorYearEmployerBenefitsForeignChild when answered, else $0 — the ordinary route, under which no prior-year benefit is brought forward. Complete on every declared item by construction, so the GreaterThan over it in ../childOnForeignPriorYearBenefitsRoute is never Placeholder.

Fact.Name: This child takes the Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet route
Fact.Description:
True when this child is a foreign child (Part I column (e)), the adoption is final (column (g)), the adoption became final DURING 2025, and pre-2025 employer-provided adoption benefits were received for this child. That is the worksheet's own population: "for the adoption of a foreign child that became final in 2025", entered only when there are prior-year benefits to exclude.
THE COLUMN (g) CONJUNCT IS STRUCTURAL, not redundant. The printed CAUTION tells a filer who checks column (e) to check column (g) as well, so in valid DATA finality-during-2025 implies column (g) — but the graph reads two separate answers, and a filer who says "final during 2025" while leaving column (g) blank would otherwise be barred by ../childForeignAndNotFinal at line 19 while lines 20 and 22 still took the route. Reading column (g) here makes the route structurally exclusive with the bar: a blank column (g) keeps the whole child on the barred path, which is the adverse and correct direction.
COMPLETE ON EVERY DECLARED ITEM BY CONSTRUCTION: an All over three complete-safe Booleans and a GreaterThan over a complete-safe Dollar, so it resolves Complete false — never Placeholder — on a return that answers none of the new questions.

Fact.Name: This child's ordinary maximum exclusion, before any worksheet route (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description: The per-child exclusion maximum on the ORDINARY route: $17,280, or the taxpayer's agreed share of it when a non-spouse also received employer-provided adoption benefits for the same child. HOISTED out of ../line19 so that the Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet's line 2 — which states the same divided rule in its own words, "The maximum amount of employer-provided adoption benefits that can be excluded from income is $17,280 per child. If you and another person … the $17,280 limit must be divided between the two of you" — reads the SAME fact rather than a second copy of the selection. One quantity, one fact.

Fact.Name: Employer-provided adoption benefits received IN 2025 for this child, complete-safe
Fact.Description: = ../writableEmployerAdoptionBenefits when answered, else $0. This is the body ../employerAdoptionBenefits used to carry, extracted so that the printed Form 8839 line 22 can add the pre-2025 amount on the worksheet route while the 2025-only figure stays available: worksheet line 8 ("the total 2025 employer-provided adoption benefits included on Form 8839, line 22, for all children") needs exactly this quantity, and reconstructing it by subtraction downstream would be a second derivation of the same money.

Fact.Name: This child's pre-2025 benefits included in Form 8839 line 22 (worksheet line 5 term)
Fact.Description: The part of THIS child's Form 8839 line 22 that is pre-2025 money: the route amount on the worksheet route, $0 otherwise. Worksheet line 5 asks for "the total employer-provided adoption benefits you received before 2025 included on Form 8839, line 22, for all children", so only a route child contributes — an ordinary child's line 22 contains 2025 benefits only. Summed by /adoptionForeignWorksheetLine5PriorYearBenefitsOnLine22.

Fact.Name: Dollars a route child answered on Form 8839 line 20, which the worksheet forces to zero
Fact.Description: The amount this child answered as prior-year benefits on Form 8839 line 20 (../writablePriorYearEmployerBenefits) when the child is on the worksheet route, $0 otherwise. On the route the worksheet is explicit — "Enter -0- on Form 8839, line 20" — and no prior Form 8839 could have excluded benefits for a foreign adoption that had not yet become final, so a positive line 20 beside a positive pre-2025 route amount is two contradictory answers about the same money. Summed by /adoptionForeignRouteLine20AnsweredExposure and refused by /knockoutAdoptionForeignRouteLine20Answered.

Fact.Name: Maximum exclusion per child, after any divided limit split (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description:
Form 8839 line 19, this child's column: "Maximum exclusion per child. Enter $17,280." Normally the full $17,280 per child maximum. BUT when the taxpayer and a non-spouse EACH received employer-provided adoption benefits for THIS same child, i8839 Line 19 splits the limit and line 19 becomes the taxpayer's agreed share (../line19DividedShareArm). This mirrors /form8839Children/*/line2 exactly, which is the Part II fix for the same failure (a co-adopter silently receiving the full $17,280). The $17,280 figure is read from /adoptionMaxCreditPerChild: the exclusion limit of IRC 137(b)(1) and the credit limit of IRC 23(b)(1) are the same indexed amount for 2025 and the form prints the same number on line 2 and on line 19.
ELIGIBILITY GATE: $0 outright when this child fails ../childMeetsEligibleChildDefinition (not under 18 and not the disabled exception) or when ../childForeignAndNotFinal is true (a foreign child whose adoption has not become final) — checked FIRST, mirroring the same two gates on ../line2. The age/disability test reaches Part III through IRC 137(d), which gives "qualified adoption expenses" the section 23(d) meaning, and section 23(d)(1)(A) confines those to the legal adoption of an eligible child, so an employer benefit for an ineligible adoptee is not excludable. i8839: "If the eligible child is a foreign child, you can't take the adoption credit or exclusion unless the adoption becomes final."
S-CORP >2% SHAREHOLDER BAR: $0 outright, same FIRST case, when /adoptionEmployerIsSCorpMoreThan2PctShareholder is true — i8839 Purpose of Form's printed CAUTION: "You can't exclude employer-provided adoption benefits if your employer is an S corporation in which you own more than 2% of the stock or stock with more than 2% of the voting power." Per return (the ownership question is about the taxpayer's employer, not any one child), so it applies uniformly across every child's column, same as the foreign/not-final bar.
WHAT THE PRINTED CELL THEN SHOWS. Line 19's printed instruction is the unconditional "Maximum exclusion per child. Enter $17,280", so a barred filer prints $0 where the form prints a statutory maximum. That is this module's house idiom for a barred chain — ../line19DividedShareArm and the pre-existing /adoptionCreditIsActive branch gate zero their chains the same way, and a zeroed line 19 carries the bar through line 21, line 24 and line 29 by the form's own arithmetic to the correct result, /adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits = line 23. It is nonetheless the first RETURN-level condition to reach a per-child printed maximum, and no fixture pins the printed or MeF binding of a barred line 19; if the filed presentation should be a BLANK Part III rather than a zeroed one, the gate belongs one level up, at the Part III section rather than at line 19.

Fact.Name: Divided exclusion limit arm for this child (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description: The line 19 amount on the divided limit arm = the taxpayer's agreed share (../dividedExclusionShare), capped at the full $17,280 per child maximum: a share can never exceed the statutory per child limit. Selected by ../line19 only when ../sharesExclusionLimitWithNonSpouse is true.

Fact.Name: Exclusion limit less prior year benefits, this child (Form 8839 line 21)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 21, this child's column = line 19 (the per child exclusion maximum, $17,280 or the taxpayer's divided share) minus line 20 (the prior year employer-provided benefits already excluded for this same child), floored at $0. The Part III twin of /form8839Children/*/line4, which floors identically: a divided-share line 19 can be smaller than a prior Form 8839's line 20 for the same child, and an unfloored subtraction would carry a negative "benefits eligible for exclusion" into line 24's smaller-of-line-21-or-line-22 arm, understating line 30 (the sum of all children's excluded benefits) and overstating line 31 taxable benefits beyond what the employer ever paid.

Fact.Name: Benefits eligible for exclusion, this child (Form 8839 line 24)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 24, this child's column = the smaller of line 21 or line 22, EXCEPT that for a child with special needs whose adoption became final in 2025 the taxpayer enters the amount from line 21 instead, and then only if the employer has a qualified adoption assistance program (../line24FullExclusionArmApplies). This is the Part III twin of /form8839Children/*/line6 with the extra employer plan condition that i8839 Line 24 attaches and Part II does not have.

Fact.Name: Special needs full exclusion arm applies to this child (Form 8839 line 24)
Fact.Description: True when BOTH i8839 Line 24 conditions hold for this child: the child is a child with special needs whose adoption became final in 2025 (../hasSpecialNeeds, the same flag Part II line 6 uses) AND the taxpayer's employer has a qualified adoption assistance program (/adoptionEmployerHasQualifiedAssistanceProgram). Both are required: i8839 Line 24 says to enter the amount from line 21 "only if your employer has a qualified adoption assistance program", and "If your employer has no qualified adoption assistance program, you must enter the smaller of line 21 or line 22." Dropping the program condition would over exclude for a special needs adopter whose employer has no plan.

Fact.Name: Smaller of line 21 or line 22 for this child (Form 8839 line 24)
Fact.Description: The ordinary line 24 amount = the smaller of this child's line 21 (the exclusion limit left after prior year benefits) and line 22 (the benefits actually received in 2025). Selected by ../line24 whenever the special needs full amount arm does not apply.

Fact.Name: This child's exclusion phaseout reduction (Form 8839 line 28)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 28, this child's column = line 24 x line 27 = line 24 x (/adoptionExclusionPhaseoutFractionThousandths / 1000), rounded to whole dollars. The phaseout fraction is per return and the form directs "Multiply each amount on line 24 by line 27", so the same fraction applies to every child's line 24 independently. $0 when line 25 MAGI does not exceed $259,190, which is the printed "enter -0- on line 28" branch. Same shape as Part II's /form8839Children/*/line10.

Fact.Name: Excluded benefits for this child (Form 8839 line 29)
Fact.Description:
Form 8839 line 29, this child's column = line 24 minus line 28: the employer-provided adoption benefits excluded from this taxpayer's gross income for THIS child after the MAGI phaseout. Equals line 24 when line 25 MAGI is at or below $259,190. Summed across children by /adoptionLine30ExcludedBenefits.
FILING-STATUS GATE, the SAME gate /adoptionLine30ExcludedBenefits takes, applied on this line because the printed form computes the exclusion here. Gating only the line-30 SUM would leave this per-child line at its ungated value, so a rendered Part III would print "29 Excluded benefits" = 4,000 in the child column above "30 Add the amounts on line 29" = 0, an arithmetic contradiction on the face of the form.
DUPLICATED, NOT MOVED. Line 30 keeps its own leading case. The two are not a second source of truth — both read the one predicate /adoptionFilingStatusEligible, which is what the C4 extraction was for — and keeping line 30's case makes line 30 provably $0 for a barred filer by its own body rather than only through this sum, so line 30 and line 31 stay byte-identical whatever the collection's state (declared, empty, or absent). With this gate in place line 30 also now falls out by its own printed rule, "Add the amounts on line 29".
COMPLETE-SAFE in the same shape line 30 uses: All(IsComplete(eligible), Not(eligible)). The eligibility fact is Placeholder on a return that answers NO filing status (measured), so a bare Not would turn this line — and through the line-30 CollectionSum, lines 30 and 31 and Form 1040 line 1z — Placeholder on that return. The IsComplete conjunct makes an unanswered filing status fall through to the ungated subtraction, which is the pre-E3 posture.
VALUE MOVEMENT, named. This line changes from line 24 − line 28 to $0 for a barred-MFS filer who received employer-provided adoption benefits. NO committed scenario reaches it: none of the 18 scenarios declaring /form8839Children answers ../writableEmployerAdoptionBenefits, so line 24 is $0 and line 29 was already $0 on every one of them. The witness is the node fixture tests/nodes/ty2025/form8839/f8839-part3-mfs-barred-benefits-fully-taxable, where this line moves 4,000 -> 0 while lines 23, 30 and 31 hold at 4,000, 0 and 4,000.

Fact.Name: Prior year employer-provided benefits for this child, complete safe (Form 8839 line 20)
Fact.Description: = ../writablePriorYearEmployerBenefits when answered, else $0, which is the printed No branch of line 20 ("No. Enter -0-."). Complete safe so an unanswered column cannot make this child's lines 21, 24, 28 and 29 resolve Incomplete and cascade into the return level lines 23, 30 and 31.

Fact.Name: Divided exclusion limit flag for this child, complete safe (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description: = ../writableSharesExclusionLimitWithNonSpouse when answered, else false (no non-spouse co-recipient, so the full $17,280 line 19 limit applies). Complete safe so an unanswered question cannot make every Part III line for this child resolve Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Employer-provided adoption benefits received in 2025 for this child (Form 8839 line 22)
Fact.Description:
The employer-provided adoption benefits the taxpayer received in 2025 for THIS eligible child, entered in this child's line 22 column. The form points at box 12 of the 2025 Form(s) W-2 with code T. The W-2 box 12 code T amount is already in the graph as /formW2s/*/adoptionBenefits, but that figure is per W-2 and Part III needs it per CHILD, an allocation no W-2 carries, so the per child amount is intake here. A return whose columns do not add up to the W-2 total is a reconciliation the graph does not yet perform.
2025 ONLY. Benefits received in EARLIER years never belong here, whatever the child: for an ordinary child they belong on Form 8839 line 20, and for a foreign child whose adoption became final in 2025 they belong in ../writablePriorYearEmployerBenefitsForeignChild, from which the Exclusion of Prior Year Benefits Worksheet brings them into the printed line 22.

Fact.Name: Divided $17,280 exclusion limit: a non-spouse also received employer benefits for this child (Form 8839 line 19)
Fact.Description: True if the taxpayer AND another person who is NOT the taxpayer's spouse (if filing jointly) EACH received employer-provided adoption benefits in connection with the adoption of THIS same eligible child. i8839 Line 19: in that case "the $17,280 limit must be divided between the two of you", and the taxpayer enters the agreed share on line 19 for that child. The Part II twin of this question (/form8839Children/*/writableSharesLimitWithNonSpouse) asks about PAYING qualified expenses; this one asks about RECEIVING employer benefits, so the two answers can differ and neither may stand in for the other.

Fact.Name: Your employer has a qualified adoption assistance program (i8839 Line 24)
Fact.Description: True if the taxpayer's employer has a qualified adoption assistance program as i8839 defines it under Employer-Provided Adoption Benefits. i8839 Line 24 makes this a precondition of the special needs full amount rule, and says the requirement applies whether or not any benefits were actually received under the plan. Per return, because the question is about the employer's plan rather than about a child.

Fact.Name: Your employer is an S corporation in which you own more than 2% of the stock or voting power
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Is your employer an S corporation in which you own more than 2% of the stock, or stock with more than 2% of the total voting power?" HELP: i8839 Purpose of Form prints this as a CAUTION — "You can't exclude employer-provided adoption benefits if your employer is an S corporation in which you own more than 2% of the stock or stock with more than 2% of the voting power." The question is about YOUR ownership stake in the employer that paid the benefits, not about any one child, which is why it is per return; and it bites before the question of whether the employer's plan otherwise qualifies is even reached. ASKED WHEN: once per return, on the employer-plan screen alongside /writableAdoptionEmployerHasQualifiedAssistanceProgram, whenever the return carries any Part III employer-benefit input. VALIDATION: Yes/No. UNANSWERED (three-state): neither printed state is asserted and /adoptionEmployerIsSCorpMoreThan2PctShareholder resolves FALSE, i.e. no bar. That default is what keeps every return filed before this question existed byte-identical, and it is precisely why the application must actually ask: an unasked filer who IS a >2% S-corp shareholder would otherwise take an exclusion the CAUTION denies. CONSUMER AND MONEY CONSEQUENCE: a Yes zeros /form8839Children/*/line19 for EVERY child, and with it line 21, line 24, line 29 and the return-level /adoptionLine30ExcludedBenefits, leaving /adoptionLine31TaxableBenefits equal to line 23 — the whole employer benefit taxable, carried to Form 1040 line 1f. It does NOT touch the Part II credit: the bar is specific to the section 137 exclusion.

Fact.Name: Employer S-corp >2% shareholder bar, complete-safe (i8839 Purpose of Form CAUTION)
Fact.Description: = /writableAdoptionEmployerIsSCorpMoreThan2PctShareholder when answered, else false. False is the conservative default until a filer is actually asked and says yes. Gates /form8839Children/*/line19 (and therefore line21, line24, line29, the return-level line30) to $0 for every child when true, leaving line31 = line23 (the full employer benefit taxable) — the printed effect of the exclusion being barred outright.

Fact.Name: Received employer-provided adoption benefits in a prior year for the same child (Form 8839 line 20)
Fact.Description: Form 8839 line 20's yes/no question, asked once for the return: "Did you receive employer-provided adoption benefits for a prior year for the same child?" True checks the Yes box; false checks the No box through /adoptionNoPriorYearEmployerBenefits. When it is true the taxpayer enters, per child, the total of lines 20 and 24 of the last Form 8839 filed for that child (/form8839Children/*/writablePriorYearEmployerBenefits). Deliberately NOT complete safe: an unanswered question leaves BOTH printed boxes blank rather than asserting No on the taxpayer's behalf.
